title: Frame: dissector table for PcapNG custom blocks
description:
The `frame` dissector has a case statement for dealing with PcapNG
[custom blocks][1], and has some hard-coding in for specific types of
custom block, currently TCP Black Box Log (bblog) and pcaplog blocks.

Propose replacing case statement with a new sub-dissector table keyed on
the Private Enterprise Number, tentatively named `pcapng_custom_option`.

Factor out bblog code from `packet-frame.c` into `packet-bblog.c`. Have
it register itself with this new table.

Create `packet-pcaplog.c` and factor out pcaplog code to that file. Have
it register itself with this new table.

This is one possible way of addressing the concern discussed in !3990 of
generalizing the handling of custom blocks. The hope is to reduce the
tightness of coupling `packet-frame.c` with every new custom block we
want to support.

There remains, unfortunately, tight coupling with custom block
*[options][2]* that exist on standard PcapNG blocks, since the current established precedent is to give
fields for supported options a `frame.` prefix and put them in the Frame
protocol tree.  This proposal treats that as out of scope.

There is also bblog-specific code in `wiretap/pcapng.c`. It may be
possible to move that into `packet-bblog.c`. This is also beyond the
scope of this proposal.

[1]: https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-tuexen-opsawg-pcapng-05.html#name-custom-block
[2]: https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-tuexen-opsawg-pcapng-05.html#name-custom-options

notes.body: Authorship info comes from !5855
resolved all threads

`tshark -2nVr` output comparison for pcaplog: [current master](/uploads/abd26e21d801e81c2ae49bfbc8ce050e/before.txt) vs [with this patch](/uploads/3af37deee7f561b9fcab48af7b5b91b4/after.txt). Using the attachment to !5855 as input.

[When I had a look at this] I didn't find a good solution for a custom block having custom options (which is used for PEN_NFLX), because this is parsed in `pcapng.c` and not in a dissector. This is not an issue here because you don't handle custom options, but may be something to think about for further improvements.

Regarding custom options having the `frame.` prefix I don't think it would be a big issue changing this. The PEN_NFLX data contains the same structure when used in a block and an option, and I think they should be shown exactly the same in UI (with it's own top-level tree item). Adding support for both custom block and custom options using a dissector table would probably solve this.

[When I had a look at this]: https://gitlab.com/stigbjorlykke/wireshark/-/commits/pcapng-custom-block-option

I should have clarified in the MR summary: when I mentioned custom options there, I meant in relation to non-custom blocks (so, Packet blocks for example). I don't know if that changes anything you describe here.

Am I correctly interpreting that you recommend custom options (for standard blocks) appear in the top level of the packet tree, *not* under Frame? That would make it straightforward to use a sub-dissector lookup table for custom options. But it also means a separate dissector for options vs for blocks. (Not a blocker, just a note.)

I would think that a custom block handler would also handle its own custom options on that block -- eg. bblog options in a bblog block.

Do we foresee a custom block from company A having custom options from company B? (to make up an example: a pcaplog option on a bblog block.) I sure hope not. If that's possible, I'd suggest that the custom block handler have its own code to handle other options; we could make Wireshark arbitrarily complex if we try to directly handle that sort of thing.

> Am I correctly interpreting that you recommend custom options (for standard blocks) appear in the top level of the packet tree, *not* under Frame?

Comments are added at the top level; other options are added under Frame.

It may be that the right place for custom options might not be the same for all custom options.  Having two separate tables for options to show at the top level and options to show in the frame would handle this.

> Do we foresee a custom block from company A having custom options from company B?

It might be *unlikely*, but it's not currently forbidden by the pcapng specification.  The various custom option types have "universal" option type values, not "block-type-specific" option type values.  The only part of a custom option value that's standardized in the spec is the Private Enterprise Number (PEN); everything else is up to the vendor, including mechanics for indicating which particular option this is if that vendor has more than one custom option.

A vendor might choose to do this with a custom-option type value after the PEN.  They may choose to have a single space for their custom-option type values, so that custom option 17 is always XXX, no matter what block it's in (which could mean that a block where the XXX option has no meaning has an XXX option), or they may choose to have block-type-specific spaces, so that custom option 17 is XXX in a block of type A and YYY in a block of type B.

So a custom option handler for a particular PEN would have to be provided with the block type for the block in which the option occurs and, if the block is a custom block, also provided with the PEN for the block and some way of getting additional information to identify the custom block subtype.

Or we could impose, in the pcapng specification, restrictions to simplify this, such as "custom options in a custom block must have the same PEN as the PEN of the custom block".

For NFLX I think it makes sense to show both custom block and custom option in the top level packet tree because they have similar content ("Black Box Log"). A user may not know that it's possible to find this data in the Frame tree, and then it's hidden.

For others it could depend on the content.

> For NFLX I think it makes sense to show both custom block and custom option in the top level packet tree because they have similar content ("Black Box Log"). A user may not know that it's possible to find this data in the Frame tree, and then it's hidden.

*Blocks* are always shown at the top level, custom or not.

*Options* can be shown either at the top level or not.

So do the ones that belong at the top level belong *before* the Frame information (as is the case with comments), or *after* it?

I've attempted to summarize this discussion in #18614, since that's the issue for handling custom *options*. I believe the final decision on that will have no issue on this MR, which is about handling custom *blocks*, so I'm resolving this discussion.
I'll suggest naming this "pcapng_custom_block" in case we later want to add "pcapng_custom_option".
